anti_overlap: Owns THE GROUND and only the ground: per-site state, visitation memory, patch heterogeneity, the annual window, and where accumulated consequence is allowed to live. Never reasons about the animal's interior — needs, condition bands, scars, disposition and refusal thresholds belong to the falconry and colony-sim lenses.

Does not judge the handler relation, per-individual baselines, or whether a bird will fly today — that is the falconry lens. Where falconry says refusal must be a diagnosis with an object, this lens says only that the object has no state; it must not argue about how refusal should be graded.

Does not reason in feedback gain, attractors, equilibria or loop stability — that is the colony-sim lens. Reason in fuel, patch, age, season, mosaic and window, and never re-derive need arithmetic or tune thresholds.

Does not judge the composed sequence: variety across 52 weeks, toast spacing, ji/mon ratio and narrative arc belong to the renga lens. Where this lens invokes the calendar it means the ecological year that makes an act timely or ruinous, never the pacing of what the player is shown.
Does not judge mechanism, gating, release windows or the arithmetic of two paths onto one output — that is the horology lens. It asks only WHERE a stock accumulates, never how it is metered out.

Does not adjudicate engine architecture, determinism, replay, ADR compliance or the agnosticism script's implementation — that is the sim-core lens. It may state that a per-site stock is semantically vocabulary-agnostic, but must not design the substrate refactor.

Does not argue about how events read to the player, story-sifting, toasts or the pause tier — that is the indirect-control lens. It argues that the board must differ; what the differences look like on screen is someone else's territory.

Not an ecology or ornithology source. Corvid behaviour and the accuracy of raven-vocab content are out of territory. Makes no claims about Indigenous cultural, sacred or governance matters — it reasons strictly about fuel, patch, season and timing as working land-management technique.
decision_lens: Where does the accumulated consequence of not acting live — in the animal or in the ground? Judge whether the world has any state that a visit changes and a non-visit lets grow; whether the board is a mosaic (patches in visibly different states, so the choice between them is a real choice) or a uniform field; whether the calendar has a window in which the same ordinary act is timely rather than ruinous; and whether the design's proposed catastrophe is a monotone decline inside one creature (which the practitioner would call a spiral you merely watch) or a threshold in the land whose fuse was lit by a season of neglect (which is danger you can see coming and act on).
distance_rationale: All six covered lenses reason about something INSIDE the system's actors or its authored sequence: the colony-sim lens owns loop dynamics between need formulas, the indirect-control lens owns the player's verb and story legibility, the sim-core lens owns engine architecture and canon audit, renga owns the composed sequence, horology owns the mechanism and its gating, falconry owns the handler's relation to one animal on one morning. Not one of them owns THE GROUND. This craft's only subject is a landscape worked in pieces on a calendar — where the accumulator lives, whether the board remembers, whether patches differ, and why a one-verb practice is nonetheless full of judgement. That is exactly the axis the target's measured evidence points at and no reviewer has picked up: `Site` carries two static multipliers, all shipped grounds are set to the identity, `site_intensity()` is a pure function of kind and day, no non-test code mutates a site, and the world's longest cycle is seven days — so the vision's own threat pillar (R3, 'a ward you stop visiting slides') has no substrate at all, while the proposed goal doubles down on the animal interior. There is no surface adjacency to mislead: nothing in RaveNous's corpus is about land management, fuel, or the cost of not going somewhere. Not an AI-cliche domain, pre-modern, non-Western, physical, and the specific tradition (annual window, mosaic age-classes, cool-versus-hot fire) is far more particular than the generic resilience-discourse 'controlled burn'.
expected_isomorphisms: health as the one accumulator every hardship routes into <-> fuel load, which accumulates in the GROUND you did not visit, not in the practitioner or the animals — so the consequence of omission sits where the one verb can still reach it
a ground whose yield is `intensity(kind.bloom, day)` regardless of visits <-> country with no fuel load and no age: it cannot be tended, cannot be neglected, and cannot reward returning

every shipped site at `richness_mod_bp = SITE_MOD_UNIT_BP` <-> a landscape burnt uniformly or not at all; the practitioner's whole product is the MOSAIC of differently-aged patches, and a uniform board is the recognised failure state

zero deaths, zero refusals, 132 identical toasts across 52 weeks <-> country where nothing has happened for a long time, which reads as calm and is in fact the accumulation phase — quiet is the symptom, not the absence of a problem

'the spiral IS the danger' <-> a monotone decline versus a threshold discharge: this craft's catastrophe is a step function whose probability was set by omission seasons earlier, which is what makes it simultaneously foreseeable and preventable

the player's only verb being dispatch to a ground <-> putting fire on a patch: a genuinely one-verb craft that is nonetheless dense with judgement, because the BOARD is differentiated and remembers — evidence that the verb is not the problem

bloom periods of 1-7 days looped 52 times <-> a calendar with no annual window: cool-versus-hot fire is the same act made right or ruinous by season, and without a long cycle there is no timing to get right

condition/health as the thing that must be watched <-> reading the grass, the fuel and the patch age to decide where to go this season: the instrument points at the LAND, and the animal's state is a lagging indicator of how the land was kept
R3's 'a ward you stop visiting slides' <-> sick country: ground choked by unburnt accumulation, which is the craft's exact name for the state the vision describes and the substrate cannot represent

`reject_reason()` receiving a site it never reads <-> an instrument aimed at a featureless field; the argument is unused because there is nothing there to read, not because the predicate forgot to look
focus: WHERE the accumulator lives. The proposed goal puts every hardship inside the animal (health as the one stock all deprivation routes into); a fire-tending craft puts it in the LAND — unattended ground accumulates fuel, and the danger you eventually meet is a consequence of where you did not go, seasons ago. Owns the ground as a stateful, remembering, heterogeneous board: patch condition, time since last visit, the mosaic as the actual product of tending, the seasonal window in which an ordinary act is beneficial rather than ruinous, and catastrophe as a threshold event whose probability was set long before it fired. Also owns the asymmetry between a richly-modelled animal interior and an inert world.
name: fd-culturalfire-mosaic-and-fuel-load
persona: Apply the perspective of a practitioner of cultural fire — the Aboriginal Australian right-way fire and fire-stick farming traditions (Arnhem Land early-dry-season burning, Martu burning for hunting, Gunditjmara and southeastern practice as documented by Gammage and Steffensen), with the comparable Indigenous Californian and Sahelian burning crafts. This is a craft whose entire subject is a landscape that must be worked in pieces, on a calendar, forever. The practitioner's only verb is where to put fire and when. It works — it built and held continent-scale country for millennia — because the board is differentiated and REMEMBERS: every patch carries a fuel load, an age since it was last burnt, and a debt. Neglect is not an absence of events; it is a stock that grows in the ground and is paid all at once. Treat this as working land-management knowledge with a documented literature, never as mysticism, and make no claims about cultural or sacred matters — reason only about fuel, patch, season, mosaic and timing.
review_areas: THE HEADLINE: `Site` in crates/animal-sim/src/world.rs carries only `id`, `kind`, `pos_bp`, `region`, `richness_mod_bp`, `risk_mod_bp` — and both multipliers are static, set at scenario build and never written again (no `sites.get_mut` outside tests). The land has NO state that a visit changes. Nothing accumulates where nobody went. Judge whether a tending game can produce danger at all when the only thing that can change is the inside of a bird.

Every ground in the shipped scenario (crates/raven-vocab/src/scenario.rs) sets `richness_mod_bp = SITE_MOD_UNIT_BP` — the identity. The mosaic is not merely ageless, it is UNIFORM: all grounds of a kind are interchangeable. A practitioner's board is patches of different ages side by side; that difference IS the tended product. Judge whether a uniform board can make dispatch a decision.

`site_intensity()` in crates/animal-sim/src/sites.rs is `intensity(kind.bloom, day)` scaled by a constant — a pure periodic function of the calendar. A ground worked every day and a ground never visited yield exactly the same. There is no depletion and therefore no regrowth, so there is no reason to rotate, rest, or return. R3 makes tending the heart; test whether the substrate can express tending at all.

THE YEAR HAS NO YEAR IN IT: every bloom period in crates/raven-vocab/src/lib.rs is 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7 days. The longest cycle in the world is one week, repeated ~52 times at identical amplitude. A fire calendar's whole structure is annual — one window per year, one burn per patch per several years. Judge whether a metronome can supply the seasonal window in which an ordinary act becomes timely, and what that implies for 'the year can hurt me'.

ADVERSARIAL ON THE PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE: routing all deprivation into one health stock builds a monotone decline inside one creature. In this craft that is not danger, it is a spiral you watch — the fuse was never lit anywhere the practitioner could have acted. Argue whether the goal is manufacturing the WRONG SHAPE of hazard, and what the alternative (accumulation in the ground, discharged as a threshold) would cost.

ADVERSARIAL ON 'THE SPIRAL IS THE DANGER' (last goal's ruling): a spiral has no window. The practitioner's danger is a step function whose probability was set by omission a season earlier, which is exactly what makes it both foreseeable and preventable. Judge whether the spiral was ever the right model, or a substitute adopted because the board had no state to put a fuse in.

COOL FIRE VS HOT FIRE: the same act, at the right time on the right patch, maintains the country; at the wrong time it destroys it. This is where a one-verb craft gets its entire decision space. Assess whether dispatching a bird to a ground can ever be right-or-wrong-by-timing here, or whether its outcome is a function of (kind, day, bird) with no term for the ground's history.

WHAT NOBODY HAS NAMED — the modelling asymmetry: animal-sim has a deep animal interior (needs, drains, env surcharges, night exposure, shelter recovery, disposition, condition bands, scars, refusal, death policy) and a nearly empty world (position, kind, two constants). Argue whether that asymmetry, not danger or legibility, is the structural bug, and whether every previous fix has aimed at the well-modelled half because that is where the knobs are.

R12 / AGNOSTICISM, AS AN ENABLER NOT A CONSTRAINT: per-site stock with a working-down rate, a regrowth rate and a last-visited tick is fully vocabulary-agnostic — an octopus vocabulary has reefs that get picked over and recover. Test whether the missing world model is actually forbidden by R12 or merely absent, and whether scripts/check-agnosticism.sh would object at all.

The refusal finding from the land's side: `reject_reason()` in crates/animal-sim/src/sim.rs takes the site but the predicate ignores it. Read that not as a bug in the predicate but as a symptom — there is nothing about a ground worth reading, so no rule could use the argument if it wanted to. Judge which of the two is the fix.

Water floors at 1837 and sits under 7000 for 59% of the year, yet is neither lethal nor in refuse_when. In this craft, a resource under sustained pressure with no consequence means the pressure is decorative. Assess whether water is the design's real, already-existing scarcity signal that has simply been given nothing to do.

132 identical toasts and a monotone surface: a practitioner reads variety off the LAND — this patch is two years old, that one burnt last season, that one is choked. Judge whether surface monotony is a readout problem at all, or the faithful rendering of a world in which nothing differs and nothing has happened.

R3 (wards drift + caches mature) is locked canon and names drift as THE threat; R5 caches are deferred. Assess whether R3's drift half has any substrate mechanism whatsoever, and whether the vision's own threat pillar has been quietly replaced by an animal-interior hazard because that was the reachable one.
severity_examples: P0: the world has no mutable state. `Site` carries two static multipliers, both set to the identity in the shipped scenario, and `site_intensity()` reads the site kind's periodic bloom regardless of who has been there — so a ground the murder works every day and a ground no bird has ever visited are numerically identical forever. This means neglect cannot accumulate anywhere in the game, which makes R3's central claim ('a ward you stop visiting slides — neglect is felt; tending is the verb') unimplementable in the current substrate, not merely unimplemented. The proposed goal routes every hardship into `health` on the animal, which puts the accumulator in the only place it CANNOT connect to the player's verb: dispatch selects a ground, and a ground has nothing to accumulate. The zero-death, zero-refusal, 132-identical-toast year is the correct output of a landscape with no memory, and no health tuning changes it.

P0: the mosaic is uniform, so dispatch has no differentiated object. Every ground in crates/raven-vocab/src/scenario.rs uses `richness_mod_bp = SITE_MOD_UNIT_BP`; grounds differ only by kind and position. A tending craft's entire skill is choosing between patches that are in visibly different states, and the tended mosaic — patches of many ages side by side — is the product, not a side effect. With a uniform board, choosing ground A over ground B of the same kind is a distance calculation, and the player's one verb resolves to routing, not judgement. This is upstream of the refusal finding and upstream of GATE 1 and GATE 2: neither gate can create a decision, because the decision needs two grounds that are not the same.

P1: the world's longest cycle is seven days. Every bloom in crates/raven-vocab/src/lib.rs has period 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7, so a 52-week year is ~52 identical weeks at identical amplitude, with no annual structure, no scarce season and no window. The goal's title is 'the year can hurt me', but there is no year in the model to do the hurting — only a metronome. A craft organised entirely around one annual window (burn early or meet a late-season fire) would say the missing hazard is not a lethal need but a long cycle: a lean stretch the murder must be carried through, which turns stores, rotation and restraint into decisions and gives 52 weeks a shape.

P1: the proposed catastrophe has the wrong shape to be actable. A spiral inside one animal is a monotone decline the player watches; the danger this craft manages is a threshold discharged in the land, whose probability was set by omission seasons earlier — which is precisely why it is both foreseeable and preventable, the two properties the goal's OUTCOME asks for ('I can see it coming and act in time'). Routing everything through health delivers foreseeability without a lever: by the time the player sees health move, the accumulated cause is inside a bird and dispatch cannot reach it. 'The spiral IS the danger' should be treated as a ruling made when the board had nowhere to put a fuse.

P2: animal-sim's modelling effort is almost entirely on the animal interior and almost none on the world, and every remediation so far — condition bands, scars, refusal, now health-as-accumulator — has aimed at the modelled half. Naming the asymmetry explicitly (a rich creature on an inert board) reframes the review's open question: the gap is not danger, legibility or agency in isolation, it is that two of the three have no substrate to attach to. A per-site stock with a last-visited tick is vocabulary-agnostic and would survive check-agnosticism.sh, so R12 is not what is blocking it.
source_domain: Indigenous fire regimes as a land-tending craft — Aboriginal Australian right-way fire and fire-stick farming (Arnhem Land early-dry-season burning, Martu burning for hunting, southeastern practice as documented by Gammage's The Biggest Estate on Earth and Steffensen's Fire Country), with the comparable Indigenous Californian and Sahelian burning traditions: fuel load as a stock that grows wherever nobody went, patch age since last burn, the mosaic of many-aged patches as the tended product, cool early-season fire versus late-season wildfire as the same act at different times, the annual window, sick country choked by neglect, burning for a purpose (access, hunting, yam, seed), and catastrophe as a threshold discharged all at once for omissions made seasons earlier.
success_hints: Read crates/animal-sim/src/world.rs `struct Site` and report every field. If the only per-site variation is two multipliers that are never written after construction, say so plainly and make it the headline.

Grep crates/ for `sites.get_mut` and `richness_mod_bp` outside tests, and report whether ANY non-test code path mutates a site during a run. Then check crates/raven-vocab/src/scenario.rs and report how many grounds differ from `SITE_MOD_UNIT_BP`.
Read `site_intensity()` and `intensity()` in crates/animal-sim/src/sites.rs and state whether a ground's yield depends on anything except its kind and the calendar day.
List every `period:` value in crates/raven-vocab/src/lib.rs and report the longest cycle in the world. Compare it to the 52-week run length and say what that means for 'the year can hurt me'.

Run crates/ravenous-session/src/bin/how_close_is_it.rs and report PER-SITE variance — how many distinct grounds were ever visited, how the visits distributed across them, and whether any ground was left alone all year with no consequence. Variance across the board is this lens's diagnostic, not need floors.

Read §4 and §5 of docs/ravenous-vision.md (wards drift, the return loop) alongside the substrate, and report the gap between R3 as locked and R3 as implemented. Do not propose the civic/ward layer itself — it is OUT of the goal's scope — but do say whether the SUBSTRATE has any agnostic place to put drift.

Check scripts/check-agnosticism.sh and state whether a per-site stock (working-down rate, regrowth rate, last-visited tick) would violate R12 or pass it. If it passes, that removes the standard objection.
Do not tune numbers or re-derive need arithmetic. Judge only where consequence is allowed to accumulate and whether the board differentiates the player's one verb.
task_context: Review together (1) a proposed goal 'deprivation reaches health, and the year can hurt me' — food/water deprivation should damage health, health becomes the accumulator every hardship routes through and probably the sole lethal need; GATE 1 = does food stay lethal, GATE 2 = deficits pull condition directly AND via health, is that double-count the intended spiral or does one path get damped; and (2) the game design overall (docs/ravenous-vision.md, 18 locked decisions, plus the murder-loop, needs-availability-and-condition, corvid-ecology, df-feel-depth and genre-influences docs). RaveNous is an indirect-control civic sim: you command a murder of named, personality-driven ravens tending a procedural city. Rust workspace: animal-sim (deterministic, vocabulary-agnostic substrate, ruling R12) + raven-vocab (pure data) + Bevy app. MEASURED: a shipped 52-week year produced zero deaths, zero arrivals, zero refusals and 132 identical toasts; health never fell below 9000; water floored at 1837 and sat under 7000 for 59% of the year; the refusal predicate fired on zero idle animal-ticks. Wanted: is routing everything through health right, what does the game most need that nobody has named, are the 18 locked decisions still serving it, and was 'the spiral IS the danger' ever true.
